candidate.rulings: docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-31: STE100 technical verbs, SQL verbs and boolean names; 2026-11-01: logical operators and SQL keywords in capitals are technical names
candidate.base: WeaverAgent docs/project/candidate-ste100-verb-dictionary-v0_6.md at origin/main 66941734 (v0.6, 2026-10-28): its 208 approved keys (E1), 40 category 2 keys (E2) and E3 keys are not copied here
candidate.admission: No entry is admitted until the operator rules on its check. Synonym check done 2026-10-31 against the operator's copy (sha256 in reference). Classes: 1 no overlap, admit; 2 exact approved match, use it; 3 near-synonym, operator rules.
candidate.extra_fields: candidate, check and note are working fields of this candidate, not ste100-scheme/1 fields; they are removed when the file is ratified

reference.senses: Approved verbs cite the dictionary entry; technical senses are written in our own words. No text from the standard is copied.

verbs.sense: To execute a program, a test, or a command.

check.found: Part 2: run (v) is unapproved, alternative OPERATE (v). Condition holds: execute (v) is unapproved, alternative DO (v). run is not a rule 1.12 category 2 example.

verbs.note: Provisional. Admitted only if execute is not an approved STE100 verb; if it is, stop and report.

verbs.sense: To make a set of changes permanent in a repository or a database.

check.found: No Part 2 entry. Near: RECORD (v), meaning 2. Already admitted by the operator.

verbs.note: Admitted by the operator. One sense covers Git and SQL; a Git repository is a store of changes.

verbs.sense: To combine branches, or to combine changes into a store.

check.found: No Part 2 entry. Nearest is MIX (v), whose meanings are about materials; it does not carry the sense. combine (v) is unapproved, alternative MIX (v).

verbs.note: Whether SQL MERGE is the same act under this sense is reported for a ruling.

verbs.sense: To send changes to a remote repository.

check.found: PUSH (v) is an approved word; its two approved meanings are physical and do not fit. Near: SEND (v). An admitted key would carry a second, technical sense on an approved headword.

verbs.sense: To get from a database the rows or values that a query identifies.

check.found: SELECT (v) is an approved word, and choose (v) routes to it. Its approved meaning fits choosing rows but not returning them. A second, technical sense on an approved headword.

verbs.sense: To add new rows to a database table.

check.found: Part 2: insert (v) is unapproved, alternative PUT (v). Not a rule 1.12 category 2 example.

verbs.sense: To change values in rows that are already in a database table.

check.found: No Part 2 entry; a rule 1.12 category 2 c) example verb and a category 19 technical noun. Not an approved word. Near: CHANGE (v), which carries the SQL sense.

verbs.note: SQL candidate. Dictionary v0.6 already has update as an E2 key (category 2 c, system operations).

verbs.sense: To remove rows from a database table.

check.found: Part 2: delete (v) is unapproved, alternative ERASE (v); also a rule 1.12 category 2 b) example verb. ERASE's approved meaning carries the SQL sense.

verbs.note: SQL candidate. Dictionary v0.6 already has delete as an E2 key (category 2 b).

verbs.sense: To combine the rows of two or more tables where a related column agrees.

check.found: Part 2: join (v) is unapproved, alternative BOND (v), whose approved meanings do not fit. Near: CONNECT (v), MIX (v).

verbs.sense: To make a new database object, such as a table, an index or a view.

check.found: Part 2: create (v) is unapproved, alternative MAKE (v).

verbs.sense: To remove a database object, such as a table, an index or a view, with its contents.

check.found: Part 2: drop (v) is unapproved, alternative FALL (v), a physical meaning that does not fit. Near: ERASE (v), REMOVE (v). DROP (n) is an approved noun.

verbs.sense: To change the structure of a database object that already exists.

check.found: Part 2: alter (v) is unapproved, alternative CHANGE (v).

verbs.sense: To discard the changes of a database transaction that is not committed.

check.found: No entry for rollback, roll back or revert. Flagged: not the same act as git revert.

verbs.note: SQL candidate. The verb is two words (roll back); rollback is the noun. Flagged against git revert.

conditions.booleans: and, or, not keep their approved STE100 meanings in prose and get no special handling (operator, 2026-10-31). Written in capitals (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, TRUE, FALSE, NULL) they name the logical operator and are technical names (operator, 2026-11-01). Inside code they are operators and are not checked. The conditions grammar stays deferred to O02-1.

qualification.sentence_limit: owed by the operator: 20 for all emissions, or 20 for instructions and 25 for descriptions
